sourceCheck: Checked the official guide, all five domain pages, scope lists, Revisions, PDF, exam page, exam guides index, Coming soon, required lifecycle pages and product documentation. AIF-C01 remains current: the exam page lists Foundational, 90 minutes and 65 questions, offers scheduling and shows no successor notice. The guide specifies 50 scored and 15 unscored questions. The Italian and German versions retire after October 15, 2026. The index lists AIF-C01 as the sole AI Practitioner guide; Coming soon lists no AIF update. No AIF-C02 announcement or newer guide version was found on the deciding pages or through AWS-domain searches. The latest revision is 1.1, April 30, 2026, preceded by 1.0, March 26, 2026. All fourteen supplied task statements match, apart from terminal punctuation. Each task has one Objectives list. Domain weights are 20%, 24%, 28%, 14% and 14%. Revisions says Amazon Q was added to objective 1.3.4 and the in-scope list, but current pages omit it and name Amazon Quick. Revisions mentions SageMaker Clarify in 4.2.2, but the current domain page omits it. Revisions says AWS DeepComposer, AWS IAM Identity Center, AWS Marketplace and AWS Organizations were removed from out-of-scope; the current list retains all four. Current HTML and PDF chapters take precedence. MCP is pinned to protocol version 2026-07-28. SageMaker Clarify, Model Monitor, Ground Truth and Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) are in maintenance and closed to new customers since July 30, 2026; existing customers retain supported access. Clarify's replacement guidance limits Amazon Bedrock evaluations to foundation model evaluation, excluding classical ML bias detection and explainability. Amazon Kendra is in maintenance, closed to new customers since July 30, 2026, and points to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases. Amazon Q Business is in maintenance and closed to new customers, with Amazon Quick as its replacement. Amazon Q Developer closed new Builder ID IDE accounts and new subscriptions on May 15, 2026; IDE plugins and paid subscriptions reach end of support April 30, 2027, while AWS Management Console functionality is unaffected. AWS points IDE users to Kiro. Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic is in maintenance and closed to new customers since July 30, 2026; AWS points to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Amazon Comprehend topic modeling, event detection and prompt safety classification are closed to new customers; qualifying existing accounts retain access and other features are unaffected. Ground Truth still describes the Mechanical Turk workforce despite its end of support. Bedrock documentation confirms Managed and Customer-managed Knowledge Bases, current customization methods, four inference service tiers and model-specific abuse-detection retention exceptions. Conflicting customization deployment requirements and RAG reference-response requirements are excluded from the plan.
notes: Eleven cards cannot split evenly within a section. Sections alternate 5 true/6 false and 6 true/5 false, producing 77 of each across the deck. B1 has 22 of each. Statement hedge words occur twice for each verdict; requirement/coverage words occur once for each. Each section has 4 easy, 5 medium and 2 hard cards, and its true/false mean statement lengths differ by fewer than 5 characters.

cards.statement: Artificial intelligence sits within machine learning in the hierarchy of AI technologies.
cards.explanation: Machine learning is one branch of AI. AI also includes approaches that use explicitly programmed reasoning.
cards.misconception: AI is a narrower category within machine learning.

cards.statement: Deep learning relies on people to hand-design the features learned by its hidden layers.
cards.explanation: Deep learning learns useful representations through neural network layers, reducing the need for people to specify features manually.
cards.misconception: People manually define the internal features of a deep learning model.

cards.statement: Supervised learning requires training examples paired with the target answers a model learns to predict.
cards.explanation: The target labels provide feedback about the expected result, helping the model learn relationships between inputs and outcomes.

cards.statement: Unsupervised learning discovers which products customers tend to purchase together.
cards.explanation: Association analysis finds co-occurrence patterns in purchase records, such as items that frequently appear in the same basket.

cards.statement: Reinforcement learning favors the next immediate reward over rewards accumulated across a task.
cards.explanation: Reinforcement learning seeks cumulative reward. It can learn actions whose benefits arrive later in a task.
cards.misconception: Reinforcement learning prioritizes immediate rewards over long-term outcomes.

cards.statement: Inference adjusts a trained model's learned weights to fit the new input it receives.
cards.explanation: Inference applies an already trained model to an input to produce a prediction. The learning of model weights belongs to training.
cards.misconception: Inference performs a new training update for each input.

cards.statement: Batch inference suits predictions that a business collects together and consumes later.
cards.explanation: Batch processing groups prediction work into jobs when the application can tolerate delayed results.

cards.statement: A collection of raw product photographs qualifies as structured data because their dimensions match.
cards.explanation: Raw images are unstructured data. Matching image dimensions does not turn their visual content into records with a predefined data schema.
cards.misconception: A uniform file shape makes image content structured data.

cards.statement: A neural network's connection weights influence how strongly its neurons affect one another.
cards.explanation: Training adjusts connection weights. Those weights control the influence of signals as information passes through the network.

cards.statement: A trained ML model is the learning procedure that discovers patterns in training data.
cards.explanation: A trained model represents the patterns learned from data. The learning algorithm is the procedure that creates that model.
cards.misconception: A trained model is the training algorithm rather than the result it produces.

cards.statement: Computer vision object detection reports where multiple objects appear within the same image.
cards.explanation: Object detection locates individual objects within an image, which helps a vision system distinguish objects appearing in different positions.

cards.statement: Amazon Textract extracts form fields and table cells from scanned business documents.
cards.explanation: Amazon Textract recovers structured data from forms and tables, which helps automate entry of business records.

cards.statement: Amazon Transcribe can identify a meeting speaker's real name through speaker diarization.
cards.explanation: Amazon Transcribe assigns anonymous speaker labels to separate voices in a transcript. Diarization distinguishes speakers rather than verifying their identities.
cards.misconception: Speaker diarization identifies the people behind the voices.

cards.statement: Amazon Lex uses a slot to represent the user's goal, such as booking a hotel.
cards.explanation: An intent represents the user's requested action in Amazon Lex. A slot supplies a detail needed for that action, such as the travel date.
cards.misconception: A slot represents the requested action rather than a detail needed to fulfill it.

cards.statement: Amazon Rekognition decides if an image meets a company's content policy from its moderation labels.
cards.explanation: Amazon Rekognition reports moderation categories and confidence. The application owner applies business rules to decide whether the image is acceptable.
cards.misconception: A moderation label is the application's final content acceptability decision.

source.title: Using the image and video moderation APIs

cards.statement: Amazon Translate supports formal or informal style selection through its custom terminology setting.
cards.explanation: Custom terminology controls translations of specific terms, such as brand names. The formality setting controls how formal the translated text sounds.
cards.misconception: Custom terminology selects overall translation formality rather than specific term translations.

source.title: Customizing your translations with Amazon Translate

cards.statement: Amazon Personalize can update recommendations as a retailer records a user's recent item interactions.
cards.explanation: For supported use cases, Amazon Personalize uses recorded interactions to adapt recommendations to a user's changing interests.

source.title: Recording real-time events to influence recommendations

cards.statement: A retailer uses regression to predict next month's sales revenue as a numerical amount.
cards.explanation: Regression predicts a quantitative target such as sales revenue. It suits estimates where the required output is a numerical amount.

cards.statement: A classification model assigns a support ticket to one of several department categories.
cards.explanation: Multiclass classification predicts one label from more than two categories, such as billing, returns, or technical support.

cards.statement: Clustering helps a retailer discover customer segments from unlabeled shopping histories.
cards.explanation: Clustering discovers groups of similar customers from their purchase behavior. The business uses those groups to understand its customer segments.

cards.statement: A rules-based baseline helps a business judge whether an ML solution adds enough value.
cards.explanation: A business compares ML with simpler alternatives to justify its additional cost and complexity. Existing rules provide a useful baseline for that comparison.

source.title: MLCOST02-BP01 Identify if machine learning is the right solution

cards.statement: A large language model exposes a human-readable internal rule path for its loan predictions.
cards.explanation: A simple decision tree provides an inspectable path of rules. Complex models need additional explanation methods when a lender needs to understand decisions.
cards.misconception: An LLM is intrinsically interpretable like a simple decision tree.

source.title: RAISP02-BP07 Incorporate explainability mechanisms into the core AI system

cards.statement: A high classification accuracy establishes that a deployed model has a positive return on investment.
cards.explanation: Business return depends on deployment costs and measured financial benefits. Prediction accuracy alone does not establish a model's financial value.
cards.misconception: Accurate predictions by themselves establish a profitable ML deployment.

source.title: MLCOST06-BP02 Monitor return on investment for ML models

cards.statement: SageMaker Canvas gives business analysts a visual workflow for training predictive models.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Canvas offers a no-code workflow for building custom predictive models from business data.

cards.statement: SageMaker Feature Store's online store keeps historical versions of records for model training.
cards.explanation: The online store retains the latest feature records for low-latency predictions. The offline store keeps historical records for training.
cards.misconception: The online feature store is the historical training store.

source.title: Create, store, and share features with Feature Store

cards.statement: SageMaker Model Registry tracks the approval status of model versions considered for production.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Model Registry records model versions and their approval status, helping teams control which versions advance toward deployment.

source.title: Model Registration Deployment with Model Registry

cards.statement: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints suit interactive predictions with low latency needs.
cards.explanation: Real-time inference serves models for applications that need a prediction promptly during an interaction.

cards.statement: On-demand Amazon SageMaker AI serverless endpoints keep compute warm through idle periods.
cards.explanation: On-demand serverless endpoints scale down during idle periods. A later request can encounter a cold start while compute starts up.
cards.misconception: On-demand serverless inference keeps dedicated warm compute during idle time.

source.title: Deploy models with Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference

cards.statement: Amazon SageMaker AI asynchronous endpoints queue requests whose processing can finish later.
cards.explanation: Asynchronous inference queues incoming work and stores completed predictions in Amazon S3, fitting requests with longer processing times.

cards.statement: Amazon SageMaker AI batch transform requires a persistent endpoint to process an offline dataset.
cards.explanation: Batch transform runs prediction jobs over datasets rather than serving requests through a persistent inference endpoint.
cards.misconception: Batch transform needs an ongoing endpoint deployment.

source.title: Batch transform for inference with Amazon SageMaker AI

cards.statement: MLOps practices automate repeated model training and deployment work across the lifecycle.
cards.explanation: MLOps connects model development with operations through repeatable workflows, helping teams manage model releases consistently.

cards.statement: Data drift describes the decline in a deployed model's prediction accuracy as time passes.
cards.explanation: Data drift is a change in the distribution of input data compared with the data used as a baseline.
cards.misconception: Data drift is a decline in prediction accuracy rather than a change in input data.

source.title: MLREL03-BP03 Validate models with relevant data

cards.statement: Precision measures the share of actual positive cases that a classifier successfully detects.
cards.explanation: Precision measures how many predicted positive cases are actually positive. It helps assess the reliability of positive predictions.
cards.misconception: Precision measures coverage of actual positives rather than reliability of predicted positives.

cards.statement: A text model counts the words in a prompt to determine its number of input tokens.
cards.explanation: Text tokens may be parts of words, complete words or punctuation. Counting written words therefore gives a different measure from counting tokens.
cards.misconception: Word count equals token count.

cards.statement: Text embeddings place passages with similar meanings close together in a numerical vector space.
cards.explanation: An embedding captures relationships in a numerical representation. Similarity between text vectors reflects similarity in their meaning.

source.title: What are Embeddings in Machine Learning?

cards.statement: Chunking helps a retrieval system return a relevant passage from a long source document.
cards.explanation: A retrieval system works with smaller portions of a document after chunking. This helps it select focused source passages for a query.

source.title: How Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases work

cards.statement: An MCP host shares one MCP client across its connections to several MCP servers.
cards.explanation: An MCP host creates a separate client for a server connection. The host coordinates these clients as it connects to multiple servers.
cards.misconception: An MCP host uses a single client for connections to several servers.

cards.statement: A transformer's attention weighs relationships between distant parts of an input sequence.
cards.explanation: Attention gives relevant parts of a sequence greater influence. It helps a transformer interpret meaning using context located farther away.

source.title: What are Transformers in Artificial Intelligence?

cards.statement: A diffusion model creates an image by progressively adding noise to a clean image.
cards.explanation: During image generation, a diffusion model removes noise to construct the requested image. Adding noise belongs to the forward process used in training.
cards.misconception: The noise-adding training process is also the image-generation process.

cards.statement: Context engineering centers on improving the wording of a single user prompt.
cards.explanation: Context engineering assembles relevant information for the current task, such as conversation history and tool information, into an LLM's context.
cards.misconception: Context engineering is the optimization of one prompt's wording.

source.title: Understanding context engineering for generative AI

cards.statement: An AI agent selects external tools according to the task it is trying to complete.
cards.explanation: Tool integration extends an agent's actions beyond text responses. The agent chooses a relevant tool to perform part of its assigned task.

cards.statement: MCP connects AI applications to external systems through a model-provider-specific interface.
cards.explanation: The Model Context Protocol standardizes connections to external tools, data and workflows. Its interface works across a broad ecosystem of AI applications.
cards.misconception: MCP connections depend on a proprietary interface supplied by the application's model provider.

source.title: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

cards.statement: An MCP client retrieves server resources as context data for an AI application.
cards.explanation: MCP resources expose content, such as documents and database records, that an AI application uses as context.

cards.statement: With token-based inference pricing, longer generated answers add to output-token charges.
cards.explanation: Token-based inference bills for the output a model generates. With the same model and rate, producing more output tokens increases that charge.
